summary: The fault is well-localized to auth-service's own token-validation path: a single sharp, non-periodic step at 14:02Z to a flat ~35-37% error rate sustained for ~2h with request_rate unchanged, observed independently at api-gateway with the identical single 'invalid_token' signature, while order-service and all other callers stay clean and shared/upstream causes (redis-cache, gateway, minting tier) are excluded. Three auth-service-relevant changes exist around the onset — dep-5710 (v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11→0.12 + rewritten TokenValidator, 14:00:00Z) and cfg-2705 (kid rotation k-2025-10→k-2026-04, 14:01:00Z) — with neither rolled back or re-published after onset. However, the decisive discriminator between the two leading hypotheses (whether the rejected population contains only old-kid/unconverged tokens vs also new-kid tokens mis-parsed by the new validator) is structurally unavailable in the reachable telemetry: caller logs carry only a trace id, no kid/iss/exp; auth-service's own store is unreachable (503); and no keys/JWKS publication record or per-pod dimension exists. The #1-vs-#2 ranking is an exact tie (H1 0.40 / H2 0.40) decided only by deploy preceding rotation by one minute, so no root cause can be confirmed and the outcome is inconclusive.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deployment: JWT library upgrade (jjwt 0.11→0.12) + rewritten TokenValidator in auth-service v7.3.0
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service v7.3.0 (dep-5710, deployed 14:00:00Z) rewrote TokenValidator and upgraded jjwt 0.11→0.12, a breaking parser API change, 2 minutes before the 14:02Z metric step. The rewritten validator applies changed acceptance semantics (clock-skew default, algorithm/kid strictness, exp/nbf handling) so a deterministic class of previously-valid tokens is now rejected, yielding a steady ~36% invalid_token rate that persists because the deploy was never rolled back. The deploy is the only auth-side change that strictly precedes the symptom and is never reverted.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0) deployed at 14:00:00Z with 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; status live, not rolled back.
The rewritten validator changes token-acceptance semantics so a class of previously-valid tokens is now rejected (HIST-109 shows this symptom class from a JWT library upgrade).
The rejected class is deterministic and fixed, so the error rate steps and stays flat rather than decaying.
auth-service error_rate steps from ~0.2% baseline to ~36% at the 14:00-14:02 window and stays flat at 35-37% through 15:55, with request_rate unchanged (no traffic surge).
The rejection surfaces to callers as 401 invalid_token; api-gateway shows the identical single-pattern signature from 14:02:22Z through 15:58:51Z (a sampled WARN stream, not the literal rate).
No rollback (rolled_back_at null) or post-onset change occurred, so the elevated rate persists for the whole ~2h window.

assumptions: ASSUMED: a breaking parser change rejects a deterministic ~1/3 of otherwise-valid tokens rather than all-or-none; no mechanism evidence exists (F18 is precedent only, F30 says the kid question is unobservable)
ASSUMED: the ~36% is spread across the fleet, not concentrated in a subset; no per-pod dimension exists (F12)
The rejected cohort is a single stable signature (F27) — consistent with a parse-strictness rule, but equally consistent with an unconverged-fleet share

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change: scheduled signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) to kid k-2026-04 without staged/dual-key propagation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2705 rotated auth-service jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 → k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z, immediately before the first 401 and the metric step. If the new kid was published without a grace/dual-key window (and none was ever configured — cfg-2705 is the only config change all day), tokens or instances still on the old key fail as invalid_token at a steady share, matching HIST-108. The rotation is a real auth-side change contemporaneous with the step, and its failure mode is structurally unverifiable in the retrieved data.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotated jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z, authored by 'security-automation', 'Scheduled signing-key rotation'; it is the ONLY config change all day (all-services count 0 before and after).
The rotation precedes the symptom: k-2026-04 publish timestamp 14:01:00Z < 14:02:00Z metric step and < 14:02:22Z first gateway invalid_token log.
Without staged JWKS propagation / a dual-key window, a stable fraction of validations fails with invalid_token (HIST-108 is the exact signature).
auth-service error_rate steps to ~36% at 14:02 and stays flat through 15:55 (single step, not periodic).
The same 401 invalid_token signature is observed at api-gateway from 14:02:22Z onward (sampled WARN stream).
The rate does not decay over 2h; the conventional HIST-108 resolution path (re-publish old key / rollback) never occurs.

assumptions: ASSUMED: the rotation had NO grace/dual-key window; the config API exposes no key-material/JWKS fields and no 'jwks'/'identity' service exists, so this is structurally unobservable (F24, F16, F21, F30)

ASSUMED: the stable share corresponds to old-kid tokens in steady-state circulation — but the rate does not decay over 2h, which weakens pure old-kid circulation and is not explained by the conventional HIST-108 mechanism
Two concurrent auth-side changes exist one minute apart; the rotation cannot be isolated from the deploy as the trigger in available data

ranked_hypotheses.title: Partial-fleet failure: one of N auth-service replicas serves bad validations (~33%)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A single bad replica (bad v7.3.0 canary pod or one pod that never loaded the rotated key) handles roughly a third of traffic and fails all its validations, matching the observed ~33-36% error share. This predicts a constant traffic share failing — exactly the flat 2h plateau observed — and cannot be excluded because no per-pod dimension exists in auth-service telemetry.

causal_chain.claim: v7.3.0 rolled out at 14:00Z; if one of ~3 replicas is bad, ~33% of traffic fails all its validations.
No per-pod/per-replica dimension exists for auth-service metrics, so the traffic split cannot be measured.
A fixed 36% step at 14:02 flatlining over 2h matches a constant traffic share routed to one bad replica; request_rate is unchanged so the share is genuine.
No decay over 2h is consistent with a constant bad-replica traffic share (this hypothesis survives the no-decay test that weakens H2).

assumptions: ASSUMED: rollout was partial/canary rather than all-at-once (only one deploy record, no rollout detail)
ASSUMED: one replica handles almost exactly ~1/3 of traffic and the other pods are healthy
ASSUMED: the flat 36% is an instance-share effect rather than a global acceptance rule

ranked_hypotheses.title: Upstream caller/gateway mints or forwards malformed/expired tokens; auth-service correctly rejects
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A caller (api-gateway or another minting tier) produces or forwards tokens that are malformed or expired, and auth-service's 401 invalid_token is correct behavior — fault origin upstream of auth-service. Its decisive axis (a token-MINTING caller also emitting 401s) was not closed: the enumeration was budget-truncated, and no minting tier is even enumerated in the service inventory.

causal_chain.claim: api-gateway had 0 deploys and 0 config changes in the window; no other service changed either (only market-data and auth-service changed all day).
api-gateway independently shows the SAME 401 invalid_token signature against auth-service from 14:02:22Z; gateway request_rate is flat so it forwards the same volume.
No recorded caller-side deploy or config change coincides with onset; the only recorded changes are auth-service-side.
A caller changed token minting without any recorded deploy or config change.

assumptions: ASSUMED: a caller changed token minting without a recorded deploy/config change

ASSUMED: an unenumerated/undocumented minting caller exists — none appears in the dependency graph or service inventory (F36, F37, F38, F39, F42), and the minting-caller sweep was budget-truncated, so this is un-closed rather than refuted

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency failure: redis-cache (shared token/session store) partially degraded
ranked_hypotheses.statement: redis-cache is the only shared component in auth-service's immediate topology; partial degradation could make a fraction of token/session lookups miss, surfacing as invalid_token on ~1/3 of validations.

causal_chain.claim: auth-service -> redis-cache (cache), flagged shared:true, owner platform; it is the only shared component in auth-service's immediate set.
redis-cache is consumed by portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service too, so degradation should co-hit them — not observed (order-service flat).
No config change for redis-cache in 2026-04-14 -> 15:59Z (count 0), so no redis-side change coincides with the step.
Partial cache degradation gets reported as invalid_token on 36% of validations.

assumptions: ASSUMED: redis failures map to invalid_token rather than 5xx/timeout errors
ASSUMED: failures would partition to ~1/3 of requests without touching other consumers of the same shared cache

ranked_hypotheses.title: Clock skew / expired signing key on a subset of instances causes invalid_token on valid tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Some auth-service instances have clock skew or a stale/expired key, and their nbf/exp checks reject otherwise-valid tokens — producing invalid_token on a subset of traffic. Requires skew to begin exactly at the 14:02 step, coincident with the deploy and rotation.

causal_chain.claim: Clock skew or expired key on a subset of instances forces expiry-check failures on valid tokens.
order-service (a nearby service) shows only a benign 38ms NTP resync at 14:38 and a 260ms GC pause at 15:42 — no NTP event at 14:02.
No restart/health series or per-pod data exists to confirm or refute instance-level skew.
A skew event would need to begin exactly at 14:02 to match the step, coincident with the deploy and rotation.

assumptions: ASSUMED: skew began exactly at the 14:02 step, coincident with the deploy and key rotation

ranked_hypotheses.title: Telemetry artifact: 401 spike partly an instrument of the identity-namespace log-pipeline outage
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The log-pipeline outage in the identity namespace distorts or synchronizes error reporting, making the failure rate look like a clean 36% step when reality differs.

causal_chain.claim: identity-namespace log pipeline down since the morning; auth-service logs unsearchable.
Metric error_rate is independent of the log pipeline and shows a real 0.2% -> 36% step; request_rate unchanged so the share is genuine, not a denominator artifact.
api-gateway (a separate telemetry source) independently shows the same 401 signature from 14:02:22Z, so the spike is not a single-source artifact.

assumptions: ASSUMED: a log-pipeline outage could alter a metrics-series step; no mechanism for this is supported

facts.statement: auth-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stepped sharply from a flat ~0.2% baseline (12:00-13:59) to ~36%, with the onset bounded to the 14:00:00-14:02:00Z window (14:00 bucket at baseline avg 0.21%/max 0.26%; 14:02:00 bucket at 37.21%) and holding flat at 35-37% through 15:55 (36.27%); a single step, not periodic.
auth-service request_rate is unchanged across the onset (~386-413 req/s both before and after), so the 36% error share is not driven by a traffic surge or drop.

api-gateway independently observes the same 401 invalid_token signature against auth-service beginning 2026-04-15T14:02:22Z: 466 WARN lines matching 'auth-service POST /v<n>/token/validate -> <n> invalid_token', last 15:58:51Z; gateway error_rate stepped 0.24% at 13:59 -> 21.06% at 14:02, holding ~21%.

The rejection stream is a single stable signature, not a mixed/random bag: 100% of the 466 matched WARN lines collapse to one pattern, all at WARN level, and sampling early (14:02:22-14:12:28Z) and late (15:52:19-15:58:51Z) shows the same cadence with identical message form, i.e. a persistent systematic class that does not die out.

api-gateway's 466 rejected-token lines contain no token attributes whatsoever (no kid, iss, sub, jti, aud or expiry); the only per-request identifier is a trace id, and a targeted 'kid' search over 14:00-15:59Z returned 0 matches.

Joining the sampled trace id '09dac90d' to the api-gateway store returns exactly one line (the WARN itself) with no companion span/request record, so the join to per-request telemetry returns only the original reject line.
order-service is NOT co-affected: its error_rate stays flat at ~0.17-0.22% across 13:00-15:45 and a targeted search for 'invalid_token' on order-service over 13:00-15:59Z returned total_matched 0.
api-gateway is the ONLY non-auth-service source of this 401 signature: order-service, portfolio-service and pricing-engine log searches for 'token'/'invalid_token' all returned total_matched 0.
Gateway request_rate is flat across the onset (~1263-1287 req/s), so the gateway 401 lines are not traffic-driven and the gateway forwards the same volume to auth-service.

redis-cache is the only shared component in auth-service's immediate dependency topology (flagged shared:true, consumed by auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service), so a redis fault should co-hit those three services and would not produce an auth-service-only 401 signature.

No deploys or config changes were found for api-gateway or redis-cache across 2026-04-14 to 2026-04-15T15:59Z, and no service in the whole day window has a config change coinciding with the 401 spike other than the auth-service pair.

Only two deploys occurred across ALL services in 2026-04-15T00:00-15:59Z: market-data-service v5.0.3 at 11:35:00Z and auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z; the auth-service deploy (dep-5710) carried 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten', status live, and lands 2 minutes before the metric step.

Exactly one config change exists for 13:30-15:59Z: cfg-2705, auth-service key 'jwt.signing.key_id' old 'k-2025-10' -> new 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z, author 'security-automation', described 'Scheduled signing-key rotation'; it is 1 minute after the deploy and 1 minute before the first 401 log.
The k-2026-04 config write at 14:01:00Z precedes the 14:02Z metric step and the 14:02:22Z first gateway invalid_token log, and no keys publication record exists before 14:01Z in any service.

No config change of any kind occurred in any service between 14:02Z and 15:59Z (count 0), and dep-5710 remains status 'live' with rolled_back_at null; there was no post-onset re-publication of k-2025-10, no rollback of cfg-2705, and no grace-window/dual-key config write after onset.
The only config change all day is cfg-2705; for 2026-04-15T00:00-13:59Z the all-services config-change count is 0, meaning no earlier grace/dual-key window was configured for k-2025-10 either.

No separate keys/JWKS publication record exists for any service: get_config_changes(service='jwks') fails not_found and the known_services list contains no 'identity', 'keys' or 'jwks-service'; auth-service is the only identity-side service.

auth-service remains un-joinable: its own log store is unreachable (backend 503 'gave up after 3 attempts') and its metric set exposes only cpu_pct/error_rate/latency_p99_ms/memory_pct/rate_limited_per_min/request_rate/restarts with no per-pod dimension; no per-instance/replica breakdown was obtainable.

The trace/span store query never executed (budget_exhausted), and targeted api-gateway field probes for 'pod', 'iss', 'exp', 'k-2026-04', 'k-2025-10' were rejected unexecuted, so 'attribute absent' cannot be distinguished from 'store unreachable' and the kid distribution and per-pod termination remain undetermined.

Historical precedents for this exact signature are auth-service-side and config/deploy-caused: HIST-108 (signing-key rotation publishing new kid before all pods loaded JWKS) and HIST-109 (JWT library upgrade changing clock-skew default); both are leads only, and HIST-109 shows the symptom class can come from either the library deploy or the rotation, so the two candidates are not separable on precedent alone.

No minting tier exists between api-gateway and auth-service: the only inbound edge to auth-service is {'from':'api-gateway','to':'auth-service','kind':'http'}, the service inventory lists no minting tier and no 'user-service' or 'bff-web', and candidate minting-tier services show no change records.

auth-service CPU is flat through the incident (~37.95% at 13:00 to ~38.14% at 15:48, missing_points 0), so the ~36% 401 rate is not accompanied by a resource-saturation signature at the validating service.

assumptions: ASSUMED: a breaking parser change (jjwt 0.12 acceptance semantics — clock-skew default, algorithm/kid strictness, exp/nbf handling) rejects a deterministic ~1/3 of otherwise-valid tokens rather than all-or-none; no mechanism evidence exists in the retrieved data and HIST-109 is precedent only.
ASSUMED: the ~36% failure is spread across the fleet rather than concentrated in a subset; no per-pod dimension exists on auth-service metrics, so per-instance partitioning is impossible.
ASSUMED: the rejection cohort is a single stable signature, which is consistent with a parse-strictness rule but equally consistent with an unconverged-fleet share.
ASSUMED: the cfg-2705 key rotation had NO grace/dual-key window; the config API exposes no key-material/JWKS fields and no keys/JWKS service exists, so this is structurally unobservable.

ASSUMED: the stable flat 36% corresponds to old-kid tokens in steady-state circulation — but the rate does not decay over 2h, which weakens pure old-kid circulation and is not explained by the conventional HIST-108 mechanism.

ASSUMED: two concurrent auth-side changes one minute apart cannot be isolated from one another as the trigger in the available data; the ranking is decided only by deploy-first ordering, not by mechanism.

ASSUMED: the api-gateway 466-line WARN stream is a sampled/aggregated record, not a literal count of all rejects (a 36% rate against ~400 req/s for 2h would be on the order of a million rejects), so cohort claims drawn from it are sampled.

ASSUMED: the identity-namespace log-pipeline outage is independent of the 401 step; no change record links it to the incident, and a log-pipeline outage has no request-path effect that could produce a 36% 401 step.

ASSUMED: the discovered topology (single inbound edge api-gateway -> auth-service, no minting tier in the service inventory) is complete, so no undocumented/uninstrumented minting caller exists that could inject malformed tokens.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The config-change API exposes no key-material or JWKS fields, so whether k-2025-10 remained accepted in a dual-key/grace window after 14:01Z is not observable in this data.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Because no token attribute is logged by any reachable source, the H1-vs-H2 discriminator (does the rejected set include the NEW kid k-2026-04 or only old-kid/unconverged tokens) cannot be decided from caller logs; the gateway sees only the already-collapsed 'invalid_token' outcome.

timeline.event: Start of the incident day window; no config changes occur anywhere until 14:01Z (all-services config count 0 for 00:00-13:59Z).
market-data-service v5.0.3 deployed ('Fix symbol mapping') — the only other deploy in the day, unrelated to the auth signature.
dep-5710: auth-service v7.3.0 deployed (author d.verma) with 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; status live.
cfg-2705: auth-service jwt.signing.key_id rotated k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 by 'security-automation' ('Scheduled signing-key rotation'); the only config change all day.
auth-service error_rate steps from baseline (~0.21%) to 37.21% in the 14:02:00Z bucket; a single step, not a gradual or periodic rise.
First api-gateway WARN line 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token (trace <hex>)' — the first observable 401.
auth-service error_rate continues at 37.51%; api-gateway error_rate holds ~21%.
Incident INC-007 reported (SEV-1): ~a third of token validations fail with 401; auth-service logs not searchable due to identity-namespace log-pipeline outage.
auth-service CPU remains flat (~38.10%), confirming no resource saturation accompanies the 401 plateau.
auth-service error_rate still 36.27%, flat plateau unchanged ~2h after onset.
Last matched api-gateway invalid_token WARN line (total 466 lines); stream shows no decay or burst structure.
Latest data: no rollback of dep-5710 and no config change after 14:02Z; no keys/JWKS publication record; per-pod dimension and token attributes remain unavailable.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back cfg-2705 by re-publishing/restoring jwt.signing.key_id to its prior value 'k-2025-10' (and, if the platform supports it, re-publishing the previous key material) — this is the safest first mitigation because no grace/dual-key window was ever configured (cfg-2705 is the only config change all day) and no post-onset re-publication occurred.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2705 (kid k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) is one of only two auth-service changes and precedes the first 401 by one minute; HIST-108's documented failure mode is exactly 'key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', resolved by re-publishing the previous key. This mitigation is low-risk and directly tests H2.

recommended_actions.action: If the 401 rate does not fall after the key re-publication, roll back dep-5710 (revert auth-service to the pre-v7.3.0 jjwt 0.11 / prior TokenValidator) — the equivalent low-risk mitigation for the other auth-side change.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API + rewritten TokenValidator) is the only other auth-side change preceding the step; HIST-109 documents the same symptom class from a library upgrade that changed the clock-skew default. Sequencing the two rollbacks discriminates H1 from H2 operationally.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the validator to emit a per-request structured rejection log carrying kid, iss, exp, sub and auth-service instance/pod id (including the reason string for invalid_token), so future incidents have the decisive attribute; the identity-namespace log pipeline must be restored first since auth-service logs are currently unreachable.
recommended_actions.rationale: The H1-vs-H2 discriminator (whether the rejected set includes the new kid k-2026-04 or only old-kid/unconverged tokens) is structurally unavailable: gateway lines carry only a trace id, no kid/iss/exp, and auth-service's own store returned backend 503. Without this, the same tie will recur.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the mitigation by re-checking auth-service error_rate and the api-gateway invalid_token WARN stream after each rollback step, confirming the step returns to the ~0.2% baseline and the 14:02Z plateau disappears; also confirm request_rate stays unchanged to rule out a traffic confound.
recommended_actions.rationale: The current symptom is a single sharp step to a flat ~36% with unchanged traffic, so a successful rollback should produce a symmetric drop to baseline; reversing the step is the cleanest confirmation of which change was causal.

recommended_actions.action: Configure a staged/dual-key rotation procedure with an explicit grace window (accept old and new kid simultaneously, with JWKS propagation verified across all replicas before retiring the old key) and make the grace-window state an observable config field.
recommended_actions.rationale: No grace/dual-key window was ever configured (all-services config count 0 before 14:01Z) and HIST-108's resolution was a staged rotation; making the window explicit and observable removes the structural unobservability that blocks H2's confirmation today.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-pod/per-replica dimensions (error_rate, restarts) to auth-service telemetry and enforce canary/gradual rollout with per-instance validation metrics so partial-fleet rollouts (H5) can be confirmed or excluded rather than inferred.
recommended_actions.rationale: No per-pod dimension exists on auth-service metrics, so the partial-fleet hypothesis (~one of N replicas serving bad validations at ~33%) can be neither confirmed nor excluded, and the ~36% share cannot be partitioned by instance.

recommended_actions.action: Add a canary gate for jjwt/library upgrades that validates a corpus of real production tokens against the new parser before full rollout, and gate deploys that change token acceptance semantics on a token-attribute canary.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5710 shipped a breaking parser API change and a rewritten TokenValidator with no acceptance-semantics gate; HIST-109 shows the same failure class recurred from a library upgrade, so a token-corpus canary prevents recurrence.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are not searchable (identity-namespace log-pipeline down since the morning, and the store returned backend 503 'gave up after 3 attempts'), so the server-side 401 reason string and the per-pod first-error time cannot be read from the rejecting component itself.

No source reachable in this investigation logs a token 'kid', issuer, subject or expiry: the api-gateway WARN format truncates at 'invalid_token (trace <id>)' and a 'kid' search over 14:00-15:59Z returned 0 matches, so the decisive H1-vs-H2 discriminator (all-new / all-old / mixed kid in the rejected population) remains unresolved.

The trace/span store query never executed (tool-call budget exhausted), so no result exists to distinguish 'attribute absent' from 'store unreachable'; targeted api-gateway field probes for 'pod', 'iss', 'exp', 'k-2026-04', 'k-2025-10' were rejected unexecuted, leaving kid distribution and per-pod termination undetermined.

No per-pod/per-replica dimension exists on auth-service metrics (only cpu_pct/error_rate/latency_p99_ms/memory_pct/rate_limited_per_min/request_rate/restarts), so the partial-fleet hypothesis (H5) can be neither confirmed nor excluded.

No keys/JWKS publication record is retrievable for any service (get_config_changes(service='jwks') fails not_found; no identity/keys service in known_services), and the config API exposes no key material or grace-window field, so whether a separate publisher existed and whether k-2025-10 remained accepted after 14:01Z cannot be shown directly.

The minting-caller sweep (H4's decisive axis) was cut off by budget exhaustion: payment-service, settlement-service, market-data-service, pricing-engine, bff-web log/error_rate queries were not executed, so H4 is closed by topology (no minting tier, no non-gateway inbound edge) rather than by its own decisive test.

Only api-gateway and order-service logs/metrics were inspected; whether the invalid_token/4xx signature appears in any other caller that could mint tokens is not established, and 'bff-web'/'user-service' do not exist in the telemetry inventory.

The identity-namespace log-pipeline outage itself could not be correlated with the incident: no change/deploy/feature-flag record for it was found in the 2026-04-15 window, so whether it is coincidental or part of the same identity-side change train is unresolved.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A per-request source showing the rejected population's kid distribution: if it included the NEW kid k-2026-04, that would support H1 (new parser mis-parsing new-kid tokens); if it contained only old-kid/unconverged tokens, that would support H2 (rotation without staged propagation).
Re-publication or rollback of cfg-2705 (restoring k-2025-10) followed by a prompt return of error_rate to the ~0.2% baseline would confirm H2 as the root cause.

Rollback of dep-5710 (revert to jjwt 0.11 / prior TokenValidator) followed by a prompt return to baseline would confirm H1 as the root cause; if the rate persists after both rollbacks, the causal locus moves off these two changes.
A per-pod/per-replica breakdown showing the ~36% concentrated in a small subset of replicas (rather than spread fleet-wide) would elevate H5 (partial-fleet failure) over both H1 and H2.
Evidence that a token-minting caller or gateway-side change injected malformed/expired tokens before 14:02Z would revive H4 and move fault origin upstream of auth-service.

Evidence linking the onset to redis-cache (e.g. co-degradation of portfolio-service, pricing-engine or market-data-service, or redis-cache config changes) would revive H3, which current data contradicts.

Evidence that the 401 step began before 14:00Z (e.g. the 14:00 partial-bucket artifact is real rather than a bucket artifact) would weaken the deploy/rotation timing premise, though no source currently shows this.

findings.statement: auth-service was deployed at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z (dep-5710, v7.3.0) with a breaking JWT library upgrade 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; status live, not rolled back. This is 12 minutes before the 14:12Z incident report.

A config change cfg-2705 rotated the auth-service JWT signing key id from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z, authored by 'security-automation', described as 'Scheduled signing-key rotation'. It is one minute after the v7.3.0 deploy and 11 minutes before the report.

Across ALL services in 2026-04-15T00:00Z–15:59Z only two deploys occurred: market-data-service v5.0.3 at 11:35:00Z ('Fix symbol mapping') and auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z. No other service was deployed in the window.

auth-service's dependency map: edge 'auth-service -> redis-cache (cache)' where redis-cache is flagged "shared":true (owner platform); edges to user-db (postgres) and kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry:false); and 'api-gateway -> auth-service (http)'. So redis-cache is the only shared component in auth-service's immediate dependency set.

No deploys or config changes were found for api-gateway (deploys count 0 for 2026-04-14→14-15; config changes count 0) nor config changes for redis-cache (count 0) across 2026-04-14 → 2026-04-15T15:59Z, i.e. the 401 spike is not accompanied by a scoring gateway/ingress or shared-cache config change in the data available.

api-gateway's 466 rejected-token lines contain NO token attributes at all: every one of the matched WARN entries has the identical form 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token (trace <hex>)'. The rejected-token cohort is a single stable signature, not a mixed/random bag: top_patterns collapses 100% of the 466 matched WARN lines to one pattern 'auth-service POST /v<n>/token/validate -> <n> invalid_token (trace <n>)' (count 466, first_seen 14:02:22Z, last 15:58:51Z), and counts_by_level shows WARN 466 / nothing else.
